stories.entry_markdown:
Span: Mar 2005–Jun 2008; documented record to Aug 24, 2011.
Anchors (slice-attributed): DS9 — EFTA00231917 (1,120 pp
probable-cause affidavit, Case #05-368), EFTA00058429,
EFTA00077923, EFTA00240536, EFTA00227381 (2,265 pp case file),
EFTA00193199 (Jun 2008 prosecutor emails), EFTA00039421;
DS1–8 — EFTA00007157, EFTA00009448, EFTA00009016, plus
EFTA00009478, EFTA00009502, EFTA00009440, EFTA00009512
(May 15, 2007 grand-jury testimony), EFTA00007253; HO — 8514,
8898, 8461, 11085, 2152, 6027, plus 1690–1693, 2150, 2148, 8614.
Endpoint: 2008 non-prosecution agreement / state plea
(HO stopping point Jun 30, 2008, HO 6027). Caveat: the signed
NPA text itself was not re-verified in the DS9 sweep; the
endpoint rests on the June 2008 negotiation emails + case file,
and in the DS1–8 slice the NPA is discussed only
retrospectively (closing doc is the undated-in-slice Acosta
deposition).
Links: 2 (breach), P1 (CVRA), P14 (Ruemmler counsel), P2
(Florida supervision).
v2.0 DS8 extension: the plea hearing itself — certified transcript
of the June 30, 2008 plea conference (EFTA00027591); Nov 21, 2005
sworn statement of the Palm Beach house manager (EFTA00029390);
Aug 22, 2006 interview of a former residence employee, resurfaced
via Oct 4, 2021 email (EFTA00029223); 1B4 evidence-box log, last
inventoried Jul 20, 2021 (EFTA00029907); the NPA instrument itself
(EFTA00013680) and the state plea form (EFTA00013890); plea-hearing
transcript (EFTA00032238) — its cover/body show Jun 20 vs Jun 30,
2008; RESOLVED in v3.0 (WS5): the plea hearing was Jun 30, 2008 — both
copies' cover pages give Jun 30, corroborated by EFTA00013678 (plea
reported the afternoon of Jun 30) and EFTA00010507 (Marra opinion:
plea entered Jun 30, 2008). Jun 20 appears only in the transcript's
own page-2 preamble and is an internal error in the document, not a
second hearing date. A DS11 copy (EFTA02729757, 51 pp.) shows the
same cover/body discrepancy.

v3.0 DS11 extension: EFTA02729079 (Apr 17, 2006, 1 p.) — State
Attorney Krischer's office confirms a settlement offer to Epstein's
counsel: the state will not proceed with grand-jury proceedings the
next day if Epstein pleads to aggravated assault with intent to
commit a felony (third-degree), adjudication withheld, 5 years'
probation, covering all allegations in PBPD case 05-000368;
acceptance was to be confirmed in writing and is not established by
this letter. EFTA02728515 (Aug 7, 2006, 1 p.) — Palm Beach PD
request for a subpoena to Cingular Cellular for subscriber
information and calls, Jan–Mar 2004, case 05-368. EFTA02729757
(51 pp.) — plea-conference transcript, State v. Epstein, certified
copy dated June 30, 2008 with the proceedings body dated June 20,
2008 (see the resolved date discrepancy above). EFTA02729808
(21 pp.) and EFTA02725847 (11 pp.) — the negotiated plea terms
sheet (two DS11 copies of the same form). EFTA02725185 (Nov 2009,
2 pp. — AUSA letter, the USAO's account of the Rothstein fraud as
it touched the Epstein cases; the AUSA's characterizations, labeled
as such; also a Story 6 extension).

v3.2 (WS5) extension — OCR-tolerant sweep legs: EFTA00186672 (DS9): grand-jury subpoena to JEGE Inc, 103 Foulk Road, Wilmington, DE, FGJ 05-02 (2005), subpoena to testify before the grand jury. Found via the CARBYNE group ("Carbine" hit is aircraft-registration OCR noise); the subpoena itself is a 2005 grand-jury item not in Story 1's anchors. EFTA00186947 (DS9): subpoena to testify before the grand jury, to the Custodian of Records, Broward Center for the Performing Arts, 201 SW Fifth Avenue, Fort Lauderdale (2007). EFTA00279466 (DS9): PBPD evidence inventory (CDs, phone messages, digital photos; case 05-368). A single inventory list; adds the evidence-handling detail to Story 1.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — negotiation chronology, filing record, and the record to Aug 2011: the NPA's signing mechanics and signature-page questions are documented to Feb 2010, and the documented record now runs to Aug 24, 2011 (SDFL office-wide recusal) via the timeline exhibit. Sep 24, 2007 — the signing-day transmission: AUSA transmits "The final Epstein agreement (I hope)" (EFTA00215028), appeals having reviewed the first "It appearing" paragraph, signed copy by fax, originals by FedEx. The negotiation chronology is indexed in "In Re Operation Leap Year Key Correspondence Volume 1 of 2 (Through Signing of NPA) INDEX" (EFTA00190101) — tab-level chronology Nov 16, 2006–Sep 24, 2007 (Vol 1, tabs 1–81) and post-signing (Vol 2), incl. the Jul 26, 2007 USAO defense summary of terms, Sep 10 Lefcourt's first proposed NPA, Sep 11 Acosta edits, Sep 12 Lefkowitz rejecting a maritime-assault plea, Sep 14 Acosta summary (plead to an Information: 1 count obstruction + 1 count simple assault), Sep 18 Lefkowitz's §1512(d) proposal and 12-month + community-control ask, Sep 19 Lefkowitz redline (waive PSI, binding sentencing recommendation, jointly recommend an incorrect Guidelines calculation, state-court Trust, plead to "coercing a person to become a prostitute", remove appeal waiver), Sep 21 registration dispute, Sep 23 defense admission of a "mistaken assumption" behind the 796.03 plea, Sep 24 final edits 1:54 p.m., signed agreement 4:26 p.m. The index is a finding aid, not the underlying letters — cite as the index's record of the correspondence. Sep 21, 2007 — Epstein "has agreed to all the terms, including pleading to the indictment, 18 months incarceration, followed by 1 year house arrest, as a condition of 5 years probation… plus a fund for the victims as Feds require. The sticking point is requiring a plea to a registerable offense" (EFTA00215169); same file: AUSA to Krischer — deadline of tomorrow afternoon for a signed agreement "or I need to indict the case on Tuesday"; defense "only want to plead to state charges, not concurrent state and federal". Sep 18, 2007 — "I know that the U.S. Attorney will not go below 18 months of prison/jail time" (EFTA00215281); Lefkowitz's alternative: one count of §1512, 12 months + 1 year home detention, then 2 years state probation. Sep 7, 2007 — AUSA circulates both drafts, "OLY_Plea_Agreement.wpd" + "OLY_Non-Prosecution_Agreement.wpd" (EFTA00013495). Sep 10, 2007 — AUSA → Lefcourt attaching the Office's written counterproposal (EFTA00067241). Jun 23, 2008 DOJ letter (Senior Associate Deputy AG) to Lefkowitz/Starr — DOJ completed "a thorough review of the U.S. Attorney's handling"; "we see nothing in the conduct of the U.S. Attorney's Office that gives us any reason to alter our opinion"; federal prosecution "appropriate" (EFTA00179250, which also carries the Dec 5, 2008 Acosta work-release notice to Brad Edwards — USAO learned of the work-release application only after Epstein had begun it, "more than six weeks after he began participating" — and the Nov 2, 2010 CVRA litigation-hold letter). Dec 4, 2007 — Acosta's reply to Starr's Nov 28, 2007 letter (EFTA00190007): the NPA's three federal interests — (1) plead guilty to a "registerable" offense, (2) binding recommendation for a sufficient term of imprisonment, (3) not harm victims' interests — "place the victims in the same position as they would have been, had Mr. Epstein been convicted at trial. No more; no less"; "the language of Paragraph 8 was [provided] to us by defense counsel." Feb 16–17, 2010 — "We have 'umpteen' copies of the NPA, but cannot find any that contain that signature to either the Non-Prosecution Agreement or the Addendum" (EFTA00213342); the signed addendum is transmitted separately (EFTA00207077, file dated Oct 30, 2007; the Second Addendum's recital says Oct 29, 2007 — both dates recorded as written, not reconciled). Jun 27, 2008 — Acosta → Goldberger/Black: the proposed state plea "does not comply with the terms of the Non-Prosecution Agreement" (18 months community control vs the NPA's consecutive 12 + 6 months county jail "without probation or community control in lieu of imprisonment") (EFTA00067456). Jul 8, 2008 — Acosta → Goldberger: on Jun 30, 2008 USAO provided a list of 31 individuals "whom it was prepared to name in an Indictment as victims"; Jul 7, another victim identified = 32 total; victim notifications to go out Jul 9, 2008 (EFTA00067249). Jul 9, 2008 — Goldberger → AUSA: objections to the victim notification (no hand service; no redacted list; eliminate the "acknowledgment" section; add the prior representation that the government is not vouching for any claim's veracity) (EFTA00067468). Jul 1, 2008 — AUSA attaches "the agreement, with addenda, for filing with the Court under seal" + flags "misstatements" during the change of plea (Florida Science Foundation incorporated Nov 2007, not "a couple of years ago"; its "office" address is Goldberger's suite) (EFTA00013914). Aug 12, 2008 — "It looks like they only filed the original September agreement not either of the addenda" (EFTA00013965). Sep 17, 2008 — AUSA → Krischer: the NPA's confidentiality provision "requires us to inform Mr. Epstein's counsel before making any disclosure — even a compulsory disclosure" (EFTA00014172). Nov 1, 2007 — DRAFT email to the State Attorney's Office: simultaneous plea + sentencing in Oct (later Nov), self-surrender by Jan 4, 2008 (EFTA00013523 — a draft, not a sent letter). The "EPSTEIN INVESTIGATION TIMELINE" exhibit (EFTA00224943, 51 pp., 6(e) material) — dated chronology May 1, 2006–Aug 24, 2011: May 1, 2006 Reiter letter; May 23, 2006 Operation Leap Year file opening; Aug 2, 2006 subpoenas; Nov 13, 2006 subpoenas to pilots; Jun 12, 2009 Marra hearing transcript; Sep 1, 2009 draft breach letter; Sep 29, 2009 letter re Epstein violating his no-contact order on Sep 16, 2009; Oct 29, 2009 "Open file and request USAO# (2009R02690, Operation Stolen Globe)"; Jul 1–31, 2010 Epstein completed house arrest; Sep 8, 2010 administrative order closing case; Mar 20, 2011 Acosta letter; Aug 2011 SDFL office-wide recusal notices (Jul 28–Aug 29, 2011). The CVRA exhibit "JEFFREY EPSTEIN Timeline-Summary" (EFTA00192978, 5 pp.) — meetings Feb 20, Jun 26, Jul 26, Sep 7, Sep 12, 2007; Sep 24, 2007 NPA signed; Sep 25, 2007 scheduled date for federal indictment; Oct 29, 2007 deadline for plea/sentencing; Jan 4, 2008 scheduled self-surrender; plus a Federal Sentencing Guidelines calculation (§§1591, 2422(b), 2423(b); offense level 36; advisory range 188–235 months) for the contemplated federal charges. Defense-side summaries — cite ONLY as Epstein's counsel's account, not as findings: EFTA00314859 ("SUMMARY": Mar 2005 PBPD investigation; the SAO prosecutor quoted as stating there were "no real victims"; the claim "the government agreed that there had never been an underage girl on Mr. Epstein's planes") and EFTA00731146 ("SUMMARY OF MISCONDUCT ISSUES": the defense's misconduct complaint against the USAO). FBI interview notes, PBPD-side account (speaker not identified in the text layer): Epstein donated $40,000 for a machine to help PBPD review security footage and wrote a $90,000 check for a fingerprint machine (not cashed) — "around the same time that the first victim had come forward" (EFTA00153737). Dec 3, 2008 — FBI Legal Attaché (Canberra) → Australian Federal Police: USAO West Palm Beach requests AFP assistance delivering a letter to an Australian-based victim referencing the NPA outcome + terms (EFTA00269841). Mar 11, 2011 — FBI EC: Mar 9, 2011 interview at USAO Fort Lauderdale with a victim + attorneys + private investigator; she "is willing to cooperate fully with any FBI investigation involving JEFFREY EPSTEIN and others" (EFTA00269912 — same Mar 9, 2011 interview as in EFTA01249058; shared with Story 2 and P46).

Span: 2019.
Anchors: EFTA02731039, EFTA00008529, EFTA02730486,

plus EFTA00008585 (v3.0, WS4: EFTA01000647 removed — Nov 11, 2014

EFTA02730486) → post-death associate inquiry.
Dated stopping point: Dec 19, 2019 (EFTA02731082);

Links: 4, 5, 10, 11.
v2.0 DS8 extension: the sealed 19 Cr. 490 indictment itself, filed
Jul 2, 2019 (EFTA00009809); Jul 8, 2019 detention conference
(EFTA00015606); victim outreach pre- and post-arrest, incl. May 24–25,
2019 Florida victim interviews (EFTA00015293) and Apr 16, 2021 /
Aug 19–20, 2021 New York victim meetings (EFTA00009834,
EFTA00010386); associate-inquiry reverse proffers Jul 2019
(EFTA00014508) and executed proffer agreement Nov 2020
(EFTA00015006); 9 East 71st St search-warrant affidavit, sworn Jul
2019 (EFTA00028388; duplicate EFTA00028499); Apr 5, 2019 attorney
proffer (EFTA00030151); Santa Monica witness interviews Dec 15–17,
2019 (EFTA00024509); nolle prosequi hearing Aug 27, 2019 — 17
victims spoke or had statements read, plus 7 more (EFTA00019994,
EFTA00031395, EFTA00031397); Sep 10, 2019 USVI-devices/six-binders
warrants (EFTA00030708); Prince Andrew MLAT pursuit stated as
intent, not a completed request (EFTA00027424); FBI summary Jul 17,
2024 (EFTA00038617); seized-device data-transfer saga Mar–Jul 2020
(20–40 TB); SDNY internal emails within hours of the death, incl.
the forfeiture pivot (EFTA00015657; see new Story P20).

v3.0 DS11 extension: EFTA02730048 (Jul 3, 2019) — arrest /
search-warrant stand-by list: 12–24 hours' notice expected when
Epstein flies into the country; rendezvous at Teterboro; AUSA brief
at noon Monday if the arrest has not happened. EFTA02730050 /
EFTA02730052 (Jul 9, 2019) — NY agents/TFOs in the Tampa area of
responsibility. EFTA02730067 / EFTA02730069 (Jul 11, 2019) —
'victim meeting' forwards with a search-warrant draft for agent
review. EFTA02730005 / EFTA02730010 / EFTA02730014 (Aug 11–13,
2019) — EAN (travel) authority for case-related travel, St. Thomas.
EFTA02730027 (Aug 14, 2019) — evidence load-up (FBI New York Rapid
Deployment Team). EFTA02730034 (Aug 9, 2019) — St. Thomas search
warrant under judicial review. EFTA02730071 (Sept 17, 2019) — status
meeting with the ADIC: victims interviewed/total, spreadsheet
tracking, CART and taint-review percentages, 3 proffers last week,
4 Florida victim interviews last week and ~5–6 planned in
California.

v3.2 (WS2) extension — the April 3, 2020 MLAT request seeking Prince Andrew's testimony (shared with P13; full text in P13's entry above): EFTA00022062 (the request itself, Apr 3, 2020, "Material Witness PA", two investigations); EFTA00032129 (draft Mar 30, 2020); EFTA00037454 (final approved version sent Apr 3, 2020, 7:30 p.m.); EFTA00031512 (follow-up Jun 26–30, 2020); EFTA00029796 (signed final circulated Jun 25, 2020). Whether the interview occurred is NOT established in DS8.

v3.2 (WS2) extension — 13 legs: LSJ search-warrant affidavit (EFTA00020141, 24 pp.): FBI agent affidavit under Rule 41, U.S. District Court of the Virgin Islands, for Little St. James Island (75 acres, ~4 miles off St. Thomas), any buildings/structures and closed containers therein; sworn before Magistrate Judge Ruth Miller in August 2019 (day not legible in the text read; the affidavit bears a "2017.08.02" footer stamp, a PDF/template artifact, not the affidavit's date — it cites flights through June 11, 2019). Probable cause as stated: international flight records show a private jet owned and utilized by Epstein traveled to or from the USVI on April 14, May 5, May 18, and June 11, 2019; the affidavit states there is probable cause to believe Epstein "recently has been present at the Subject Premises." Items to be seized include documents/communications with or regarding victims or potential victims, photographs of victims or co-conspirators, nude/partially nude or sexually suggestive photographs of individuals who appear to be teenage girls or younger, documents evidencing co-conspirators' presence, and computer devices/storage media (or copies). LSJ execution-day brief (EFTA00019669, 13 pp., Aug 12, 2019): FBI New York, Criminal Division Branch C, Squad C-20, case 31E-NY-3027571 — "On 12 AUGUST 2019, FBI NYO Criminal Branch C will execute the search warrant for Little Saint James Island (LSJ), USVI, USA." Written as a pre-execution brief, so the completed search is documented as planned-and-briefed for August 12, not by a post-search return in DS8. Silent hit enabling the arrest (EFTA00037742, 1 p.): July 5, 2019 — "SILENT HIT" on an advance passenger information query: Epstein reported arriving KTEB July 6, 2019, 17:20, flight N212JE. The notification that set up the July 6 arrest. Feb 13, 2020 attorney proffer (EFTA00025091, 7 pp.): SDNY's written reply to follow-up questions from a February 13, 2020 attorney proffer by a former Epstein staff member (identity redacted in the text read; later Maxwell's assistant). The profferer's account as stated: hired via a headhunter after a missed New York Knicks event-planning opportunity; interviewed by Maxwell, then Epstein; trained by Epstein's then-assistant; told massages were part of Epstein's normal day ("Akin to someone going daily to the gym"); Maxwell told her not to fraternize with Epstein's business associates/friends; Epstein reprimanded her for breaking that rule at a party. The account is the profferer's, not adopted as fact. Austria landing, March 22, 2019 (EFTA00037299, 2 pp.): USMS email, June 18, 2019 — Austria confirmed Epstein's plane, Epstein himself, and three females landed and spent a couple of hours in Austria on March 22, 2019 (via the Vienna RSO). A concrete pre-arrest travel datapoint; no names or ages are stated in the email. Also a P7 extension. Nov 30, 2021 prep notes (EFTA00016590, 3 pp.): a former Epstein employee recalls an address book at the Palm Beach residence (dark blue or black, "a bit bigger than a big iPhone, very thick," an estimated 200–300 pages, blank cover, black ink on white paper), first seen around 1994–1995, "different from the Rolodex." Single-witness recollection, not corroborated by a produced book in DS8. Bank productions: JPMorgan Chase production letter, November 23, 2021 (EFTA00014877 — production sent via FIR, SDNY letter attached); Deutsche Bank production follow-up, November 20, 2019 — a mislabeled file in the prior day's submission, corrected copy attached (EFTA00015935). Both are production legs in the criminal investigation, not the civil settlement (P27). Evidence logs: FD-1087 collected-item logs, March–April 2021 (EFTA00029895, EFTA00029899, 4 pp. each) — massage tables (items 1B130–1B134, beige/brown/peach/green) split from FBI Miami case 31E-MM-108062 to 50D-NY-3027571. Evidence-inventory class. Case-build admin: call with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Georgia re Epstein, March 7, 2019 (EFTA00009889 — pre-indictment coordination); "JE, first_indictment.docx" circulated July 1, 2019 (EFTA00030237 — indictment drafting leg, the day before filing); LSJ tip email, August 12, 2019, 23:04 (EFTA00037809, 3 pp.) — an island worker's tip passed to the FBI the day of the search ("Bluebeach, (Old life guard stand)… should hold some financial records, if it wasn't wiped"; Epstein's office in American Yacht Harbor "should have a lot of info as well") — a single tip, no follow-up in DS8; "Epstein Co-conspirator pies" email, August 19, 2019 (EFTA00037630 — attachment-only stub; the attachment is not in the text layer).

v3.2 (WS5) extension — OCR-tolerant sweep legs: EFTA00090773 (DS9, 39 pp): FD-302, Jul 23, 2019 (SOD-NY-3027571, Serial 168): witness interview recording that Epstein said porn websites "have the best poses for models" and that email addresses Epstein used were jepstein@yahoo.com and joepstein@yahoo.com. Post-arrest witness interview. Witness-identifying detail is redacted in the text; none is reproduced here. EFTA00159321 (DS9, 11 pp): FD-302, Nov 26, 2019, proffer-agreement interview, West Palm Beach: same content family (modeling statements; jepstein@yahoo.com and jeepstein@yahoo.com). EFTA00134151 (DS9, 387 pp): FD-302 (date of entry Dec 9, 2019): pursuant to a federal grand-jury subpoena served by SDNY, JPMorgan Chase provided the attached response dated Sep 16, 2019 (90A-NY-3151227-GJ). The 2019 case's bank-records subpoena, documented by 302. EFTA00080349 (DS9, 24 pp): Jul 8, 2019 detention-hearing transcript, 19 Cr. 490 (RMB), before Magistrate Judge Henry B. Pitman. EFTA00028785 (DS9, Jul 12, 2019): SDNY letter to Judge Berman (19 Cr. 490). EFTA00095871 (DS9, Jul 11, 2019): Reid Weingarten (Steptoe) letter to Judge Berman.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — case-opening mechanics (endpoint unchanged; the new legs are pre-history and mid-span, not endpoint-moving): Dec 19, 2018 — SDNY email: ODAG authorization to move forward with the investigation; SDFL considers itself "fully conflicted and walled off" from any Epstein investigation (due to the NPA + the ongoing lawsuit against the district); Florida FBI agents willing to give access to investigative materials but concerned about doing so without SDFL USAO knowledge (EFTA00068206). FBI Executive Summary, ~Aug/Sep 2019 (EFTA00147428, 6 pp.): case initiated 12/06/2018 after SDNY contacted FBI NY; ~60 victims identified, "potentially hundreds unidentified"; FBI NY interviewed over 20 victims; abuse reported at NY, Florida, Little St. James, New Mexico; FBI hotline: 147 leads (25 victim leads, 4 determined victims, 7 pending; 3 co-conspirator leads; 5 recruiter leads; 7 witness leads); co-conspirators: "All were served except one, who resides in London" (the London co-conspirator is not named in the document; do not name her from it); NY residence appraised $86,250,000 (Jul 13, 2019); AMEX + Deutsche Bank subpoenas — "no significant findings to report" from the flow at that point; digital evidence: 3 devices inaccessible due to encryption, 3 iPads + 1 iPhone sent to ERF for unlocking, 1 iMac locked, 1 external hard drive encrypted; Aug 10, 2019: Epstein's death, C-19 assault investigation launched; Aug 12, 2019: St. Thomas search warrant execution planned with ~60 personnel. Jun 28, 2019 — FBI Significant Case notification, case 31E-NY-3027571, opened 12/06/2018: "On 7/2/2019, SDNY has tentatively planned to charge Epstein under a sealed indictment on two counts of 18 USC 1591" (EFTA00146962). Jul 2, 2019 — FBI situation note (pre-indictment): "It is anticipated that on July 2, 2019, Jeffrey Epstein will be indicted on two counts of 18 USC 1591" (EFTA00037799). Jul 6, 2019 — SDNY internal email, indictment/detention-memo drafting (EFTA00083658): Berman's edits on the NPA description; "all of the conduct is timely charged, pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 3283"; "Judge Moses signed the search warrant this morning"; "FBI received a flight manifest from CBP last night. The passengers listed are Epstein and two pilots." Jul 3–5, 2019 — "Epstein Arrest / Search Warrant Stand-By List" briefing (EFTA01653215, 5 pp.): NPA guidance to agents — "If individuals who are approached… say that he—or they—have immunity, or can't be prosecuted because of that agreement, that is incorrect. The non-prosecution agreement does not apply to the Southern District of New York, and even if it did, we are charging conduct beyond the scope of that agreement." Approaches planned immediately after arrest: Leslie Groff, Ghislaine Maxwell, Jean Luc Brunel, Leslie Wexner — "All of these individuals should receive subpoenas." (Wexner is listed as a planned approach — association only; no allegation of wrongdoing is made in this document.)

stories.title: MCC detention and death
stories.endpoint:
death Aug 10, 2019. Cause/manner of death are now
established at OCME-relay level: Aug 11, 2019 SDNY email summary
of the autopsy (EFTA00020165 — findings consistent with
strangulation/hanging; broken hyoid, OCR-rendered "hiatal"; "no
reason to suspect that Epstein did not hang himself") and the
Aug 16, 2019 OCME conclusion relayed via SDNY (EFTA00031006 —
"OCME has officially concluded Epstein's cause of death was
hanging and the manner of death was suicide"). The OCME
report/certificate themselves are not in range; the conclusion
is relayed in the Aug 16 email, not quoted from the report.
The investigation itself remains an open end (OIG draft report
Mar 2023, EFTA00035986; guards' prosecution is Story 24). Note: the Aug 19
TRUINTEL record is post-death institutional record, not death
evidence. The MCC documents in this entry are DS8 material (see the
attribution correction above), surveyed in v2.0; the v1 claim that
death was established in the DS1–8 slice only via the DS12 summary
EFTA02730486 was wrong on attribution.

Hughes, Ph.D., ABPP (clinical psychology), 2020 (EFTA00024760, 7 pp.) — government expert witness in the Maxwell trial (file copy; whether she testified is not established from this document). stories.title: DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility investigation of the 2008 NPA
stories.endpoint:
Nov 2020 OPR Executive Summary. Findings as stated in the
summary: OPR did NOT find professional misconduct by Acosta or the
other subjects in resolving the investigation through the NPA, and did
not find evidence the decision was based on corruption or impermissible
considerations such as Epstein's wealth, status, or associations;
Acosta resisted defense efforts to return the matter to the state and
refused to eliminate incarceration and sex-offender registration;
the Oct 2007 "breakfast meeting" did not lead to the NPA, signed weeks
earlier. OPR DID conclude Acosta exercised poor judgment in resolving
the federal investigation through the NPA ("a flawed mechanism for
satisfying the federal interest") and poor judgment in failing to
ensure victims were notified about the state plea hearing. The full
OPR report is not in DS8 — only the executive summary and the draft's
processing trail; findings are reported as the summary states them.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — interview transcript + intake + jurisdiction (span unchanged, Dec 2010–Nov 2020; the Apr 2008 item below is a prologue leg, not a span move — coordinator's decision, see changelog §8): OPR interview of R. Alexander Acosta, Oct 18, 2019, Washington, D.C. — 412 transcript pages across four Bates ranges: EFTA00009229 (DS7, 100 pp., pp. 1–100), EFTA00009329 (DS7, 99 pp., pp. 101–199), EFTA00009116 (DS7, 113 pp., pp. 300–412) (pp. 200–299 = EFTA00009016, already WS5-sampled and Story 1-anchored as DS1-8). Acosta is told he is a subject: OPR is investigating (1) whether prosecutors committed professional misconduct by entering the NPA, and (2) Judge Marra's Feb 2019 finding that the government violated the CVRA. Passages read: Acosta on witness assessment ("these girls are young. They're impressionable. They are scared. Will they stand up in court?"); on balancing ("we also thought it was very important that he serve some real punishment, and that he register… a lot of people are going to be questioning for a long, long time, but that's how we balanced it"); on the CEOS critique relayed by OPR counsel ("I'm not thrilled about the agreement… Epstein is getting a much better deal than the average defendant… I would have taken the guy to trial unless the victims were clearly against it"). Read at head/tail depth, not cover-to-cover. Jan 4, 2011 — "Call from OPR" (EFTA00206528, DS9, 1 p.): OPR is in "preliminary stages of determining whether the matter should be opened into an investigation" re Cassell's request; OPR asked for (1) memos/emails showing the decisional process for entering the NPA, including opposing views, and (2) documents showing whether the FBI was made aware of the NPA negotiations (Cassell claims the FBI was kept completely out). The OPR intake leg. Apr 21, 2008 — AUSA's OPR self-report of conflict of interest (EFTA00208240, DS9, 3 pp., prologue leg): during pre-indictment plea negotiations the AUSA provided Epstein's counsel a series of possible attorneys for victims' civil-damages counsel, including Humberto Ocariz, "a friend of my boyfriend" (later "a friend of a close friend"); Epstein's counsel selected Ocariz; after conferring, the office decided it should not select victims' counsel and a Special Master (pro bono) would; Ocariz was NOT selected. The AUSA self-reports the allegation. The memo also narrates Operation Leap Year background: 25+ minor victims identified; PBPD → State Attorney → FBI → USAO; state grand jury indicted only 3 counts of solicitation of adults; indictment package prepared; counter-proposal (state plea + sex-offender registration + jail + damages); Acosta meeting; appeal to Washington (2 weeks); two-track drafting (NPA + federal plea agreement/information). Aug 24, 2020 — OPR planning to invite all known Epstein victims to a meeting "in order to announce the results of OPR's investigation into SDFL's non-prosecution agreement with Epstein" (EFTA00032211, DS8, 1 p.). Jan 29, 2019 — OIG letter (Horowitz) to 15 House members (EFTA00811997, DS9, 2 pp.): OIG does NOT have jurisdiction over DOJ attorneys' litigation/legal decisions; exclusive jurisdiction is OPR (IG Act §8E(b)(3)); OIG has objected to this limitation for 30 years. Explains why OPR, not OIG, investigated the NPA. Note: the OPR Executive Summary copies (EFTA00011475 / EFTA00013359 / EFTA00023059 / EFTA00095558 / EFTA00095727 / EFTA01250797 / EFTA01726257) are multiple copies of one summary; EFTA00011475 + EFTA00013359 are already Story 25 anchors. The summary's findings as read: all five subjects did NOT commit professional misconduct re the NPA's development/negotiation/approval; BUT OPR concludes Acosta's decision to resolve the investigation through the NPA "constitutes poor judgment" ("a flawed mechanism for satisfying the federal interest"); Acosta exercised poor judgment in failing to make certain the state would notify victims about the state plea hearing; victims "were not treated with the forthrightness and sensitivity expected by the Department."

No row states the MOU was signed in Shanghai in September; negotiation demonstrably continued after the visit (Sep 10 MOU draft, main 7449; Oct 11 SAIL revision, main 8663; Oct 15 updated MOU, main 8927) — so the September signing did not happen, or at least is not documented. Oct 15, 2015 — MOU text agreed, signature pending SAIL internal approval: main 9943 (Goldwasser→Jiang: "we agree to the latest version of the MOU you sent us. If you wish me to sign it and send it to you I will do so. If you first wish to have it approved internally on your side, please let me know when the MOU is approved and signed by you."); main 8927 (SAIL's revisions — SAIL Group definition, the foreign-shareholder clause, exclusivity "in China"; counsel Barasch: "Unless E&Y disagrees, I'd suggest signing as is" — a recommendation to sign, not a signature); main 8951 (SAIL side, Oct 11: "we believe that we are quite close to the goal of signing the MOU"). Oct 25–29, 2015 — SAIL delegation visit to Israel planned (main 9943: arrival late Oct 25, meetings and company visits Oct 26–29, a Weizmann Institute laboratory visit, a tour Fri Oct 30, meetings with the Israeli VC community; earlier main 8834 and main 9140, Oct 8: the delegation had not yet received visas); completion NOT established — no arrival, meeting, or debrief row was found in rows read. Dec 2015 — Advisory Services Agreement + Side Letter drafting; Barak–Jiang telcos: main 4810 (Dec 14, revised draft of the Advisory Services Agreement; "the language in 1.3 and 1.4 reflects the MOU", "the budget was agreed in the MOU", "SAIL says that the term was agreed between E.B. and SAIL's chairman", "E.B. and Benad were removed as parties from the agreement"); main 5017 (Dec 15, Goldwasser wants the revised agreement sent "as soon as possible (today!)" before his Shanghai visit in two weeks); main 4844 (Dec 10, term dispute — Barak and Jiang had agreed in Shanghai in June that the initial term is 3 years, extendable to 5; SAIL says the term is a "key issue"); main 6633 (Dec 27, SAIL sent a "Key Issues List" Dec 24; Goldwasser to fly to Shanghai Jan 3, 2016, meetings Jan 3–6 — the trip's outcome is not in rows read; there are NO SAIL rows at all between Dec 27, 2015 and Feb 23, 2016); main 6353 (Dec 21, Barak↔Jiang telcos Dec 14–21, 2015; Jiang "authorized our team to discuss with Professor [Goldwasser] when they meet early January of 2016 in Shanghai"). Feb 19 – Mar 13, 2016 — strain and dispute at cutoff: main 3131 (Feb 19, Barak→Jiang: "I've met several hurdles and obstacles in my relationship with Prof. Goldwasser"); main 4118 (Feb 23, Goldwasser→Barak: "We are advancing with SAIL towards closing of the fund yet there are open issues between us that we need to resolve" — staffing and a budget adjustment; "I understand that you have reservations."); main 3191 (Mar 10, SAIL's business-issues list on the Side Letter and Advisory Services Agreement — EBG ownership, SAIL: "we have been informed Mr. Barak will own about 20% shares of EBG; and Prof. Goldwasser will have 35-40%" — attributed to SAIL, not verified; non-compete survival; the IP-acquisition model; advisory fees, Q1 $625,000, Q2–Q4 $569,444 each, Year-1 formation costs $166,667 — negotiation figures, not payments; payment timing vs Chinese offshore payment rules; a $2M Year-2 budget with termination as the fallback; Goldwasser's draft replies call SAIL's proposals "offensive, disharmonious and insulting" and invoke "The MOU provided for a firm 3 year commitment"); main 2613 (Mar 13, counsel advises sending the sharp reply only to Dr. Jiang, without CC, so as not to cause him loss of "face"; a Mar 14 conference call was scheduled). Kuhn's role: adviser to Barak/Goldwasser, deliberately unnamed during the MOU process, expecting to oversee China-side JV operations once the MOU was signed (main 7393 and main 9051); Kuhn met Jiang Jun 30/Jul 1, 2015 (main 11670 and main 11769). Tier stays confirmed — the collaboration arc (two completed visits in 2015 + MOU negotiation + definitive-agreement drafting) is documented; the endpoint is now the Mar 13, 2016 cutoff in active dispute.

v3.3 (WS2) extension — MOU drafts now parsed from the mailbox attachments (endpoint and tier unchanged — confirmed; the collaboration arc is documented; the endpoint is the cutoff in dispute, not a signed deal): MOU v1 (May 18, 2015, main 11305, GKH-LAW #5997335v1) — parties: Shanghai Alliance Investment Co. Ltd. ("a private equity and venture capital arm of Shanghai Municipal Government"), Mr. Ehud Barak, Prof. Benad Goldwasser — acting through a company to be established by them ("the Company", later EBG). Recitals: SAIL "desires to dedicate an aggregate of three hundred million United States Dollars (US$300,000,000)" over five years to acquire rights in technologies from Israeli healthcare and life sciences companies ("Target Companies"); §1 "copy paste" model: SAIL or Portfolio JVs acquire **exclusive technology rights in China**, including future developments/improvements and associated production files and technology transfer; China only; Portfolio JVs prohibited from selling products based on the Technology Rights outside China; **no ownership stakes either way**; SAIL's prior consent required for every acquisition. §3 consideration: **3.1** annual fee "[three million United States Dollars (US$3,000,000)]" for an initial five-year Term, based on a pre-approved budget; **3.2** the Company is a founder of each Portfolio JV and receives **20% ownership interest without making any capital contribution**, plus minority protection and anti-dilution rights; **3.3** if SAIL/affiliates/portfolio companies invest directly in Israeli companies during the Term, the Company gets **20% of the profit**; **3.4** if SAIL acquires a company (or its technology) introduced by Barak/Goldwasser, then **[X%] of the total aggregate purchase price** (percentage blank); **3.5** if SAIL enters into any agreement with an introduced company, then **[X%] of the payments** (percentage blank). §5 non-circumvention: Term + 24 months. §6 non-binding: except §§3.3–3.5, 4, 5, 7, the MOU is non-binding; the parties agree to negotiate the Definitive Agreements in good faith within sixty (60) days. §7: governing law Hong Kong; CIETAC arbitration, Beijing, English. **Signature block: date "May __, 2015"; SAIL address blank; Barak's and Goldwasser's Israeli I.D. numbers blank; signature lines and SAIL "Chop" line blank. No signatures, no chop, no date. An unsigned draft.** EY-comments version (May 28–29, 2015, Gmail11/Sent!4/1 (315) — the parent message survives only as the Gmail11 Sent copy, Barak→Nili May 29, 2015; **no main-DB row** — cited as a file-level anchor with that caveat, not as a DB row): Goldwasser forwards Amit Oring's (EY) May 28 email: "Pls find the MOU with our comments. Plus a clean version." Changes vs v1: "Founders" terminology introduced; §2 expanded into "Efforts" (Shanghai travel, board seats, Shanghai tech hub); **annual fee raised $3,000,000 → $4,000,000** (still bracketed as a draft figure); §3.2 reworded to shares-or-option for 20% of each Portfolio JV (zero exercise price); §3.3 narrowed to investments in companies *introduced by* Barak/Goldwasser; new §3.6 (consideration survival); new **§6 Exclusivity: "The Company shall be SAIL Group's exclusive representative in Israel in the healthcare, life science, medical device and pharmaceuticals sectors during the Term."** Signature block again blank. Unsigned draft. SAIL's comments on v19 (Aug 5, 2015, main 8034 — Yun Jiang→Goldwasser; "Attached please find our comments for the draft MOU"): SAIL wants a guarantee that it is EBG's exclusive representative in China in the same sectors; SAIL wants its already-contacted Israeli companies listed as an Exhibit as exclusivity exceptions; **Key Person:** Barak and Goldwasser named as Key Persons, each to "devote substantially their business time and attention to the activity of EBG"; if either ceases to do so (a "Key Person Event"), "the collaboration between the parties shall end."; SAIL proposes EBG introduce **at least 100 projects per year**, paced quarterly; SAIL wants EBG's share (the X% in §§3.3–3.5) set "with the reference of the regular practice in the field", and a **maximum proportion** (cap) stated; SAIL proposes a second structure — Israeli hi-tech companies contribute IP/knowhow to form the Portfolio JV with the Chinese partner — and SAIL/related Chinese companies want to **reserve the right to acquire ownership stakes in the Israeli hi-tech target companies** (against v1's no-stakes rule); the Israeli counterpart should be confirmed as EBG; since EBG "is not formed at the moment", the Founders sign the MOU and assign all rights/obligations to EBG once established; the 60-day Definitive Agreements target is "a tight schedule". The $3M/$4M and 20%/X% figures were internal draft positions — Goldwasser to Kuhn, May 28, 2015 (main 12855): the exact numbers "have not [been] discussed with" SAIL. GKH's engagement proposal for the MOU/definitive-agreement work recorded May 27, 2015 (main 12677). **Signature is still NOT established**: every parsed version is an unsigned draft; no signed MOU, signed Advisory Services Agreement, or payment is in rows read. DOJ corpus: "Shanghai Alliance" scores 0 hits; no SAIL MOU material found. Coverage limit carried: the Sep–Dec 2015 MOU versions (main 7449, 8663, 8927), the Dec 2015 Advisory Services Agreement drafts (main 4810, 5017), the Key Issues List (main 6633) and Budget_EBG_v3.xlsx (part02:341) sit in Gmail01/02/03/04 zips, which do not survive on disk; their contents were not parsed. If those zips are ever recovered, the Oct 15 updated MOU and the Dec 2015 Agreement drafts are the next parse targets.

I sincerely hope you'll be able to attend SPIEF 2015. I think the Forum would benefit from your active participation in the program. My team will send you the official invitation next week. We'll also send you a list of people you might be interested in meeting with while in Saint Petersburg."** Barak replies the same evening: "Hi Sergey I'm trying to reach you over the phone and fail. I'll call you again in two hours." **The Barak–Belyakov meeting was held Apr 22, 2015** (Belyakov's own words, the day before this exchange); the formal invitation followed, as promised, on Apr 28 (part02:1161), which itself refers to "the 2 sessions which we discussed in NYC last week" — the Apr 22 meeting was in New York. April 22nd at 7pm (instead of lunch on 23rd). Wed. April 22, 2015 NY: 12:00pm Appt w/Sergey Beliakov, 7:00pm DINNER w/Ehud."** So Apr 22, 2015 in New York: Beliakov appointment at noon, dinner with Barak at 7pm — the meeting Belyakov thanks Barak for the next day was the noon appointment. Of course I will pay normal fees."** Two days after Colom's May 2, 2014 identification of Beliakov as the SPIEF organizer (EFTA00683972, already anchored); "your conference" is not named in the row. (EFTA02585722; follow-ups EFTA01748708 / EFTA01803880 / EFTA01918274 — scheduling only; the call itself is not confirmed in rows read). Will you have Time to see him?"); EFTA02353114 (Oct 24: Beliakov "asking if you could meet later as he is landing a= 520pm!", Epstein: "evenbing 25"); EFTA02227521 (Oct 24, 17:37: "830pm October 25th confirmed Sergey Beliakov"); EFTA02228152 (Oct 25, 20:54 schedule: "8:30pm Appt w/Sergey Beliakov and Yulia, his wife (he lands at 5:20pm)"); EFTA02228100 (calendar alert for the same 8:30pm Oct 25 appointment). This extends the Beliakov contact record to Oct 2017 — the latest Beliakov date in the corpus set. **Variant correction (WS3 §2.1):** the v3.2 entry's "'Beliakov' is a Belyakov spelling variant not previously recorded" stands as a variant note, but WS5 §2.3's "Beliakov — the dominant mailbox spelling of Belyakov (109 docs vs 58 for 'Belyakov')" is wrong as stated: measured across all five Barak DBs, the mailbox contains **Beliakov 0 times and Belyakov 109 times** (51 main + 10 part01 + 48 part02 — the 109 is the *Belyakov* mailbox count); the DOJ corpus contains **Beliakov 112 and Belyakov 59**. stories.entry_markdown:
Span: 2009–2019.
Anchors: EFTA00230786 (Jun 12, 2009 SDFL "willfully violated
Term 8" letter, 1,131 pp).
Endpoint: the Jun 12, 2009 breach declaration (document-verified).
Dated stopping point: Jun 12, 2009 (EFTA00230786) is the endpoint; the documented record runs to Sep 26, 2011 (EFTA00205768) — the 2010–2011 investigation is now its own story, P46.
DOWNGRADED in v3.0 (WS4): confirmed → probable. Two v2.1 anchors do
not support the story and were removed — EFTA00039665 (May 21, 2021
email forwarding a Knight Capital / SEC whistleblower appeal; nothing
about the NPA, breach, or federal inaction) and EFTA00039367 (Sep 17,
2019 BOP psychological-reconstruction memo; post-death, nothing about
the 2009 breach or the 2009–2019 period). The "no federal prosecution
until the July 2019 case" half has no supporting anchor at all and is
bounded here as an unanchored claim, not a verified finding — it rests
on the slice + prior findings, not a search of all federal dockets.
v3.1 narrows the title/endpoint to the breach declaration alone. A
confirmed tier for that narrowed story would be defensible on its two
anchors, but the tier is kept probable pending review — the v3.0
downgrade was the correction, and re-tiering it is a review decision,
not taken unilaterally in a fix pass.

Open lead (partly answered in v3.3 — see P46): whether no federal prosecution followed the breach declaration until the July 2019 case, and why — the "decade of inaction" question. For 2010–2011 it is now answered in part: a new criminal investigation with victim interviews was opened (Jul–Oct 2010) and a preliminary investigation ran to Mar 2011, then the USAO declined to move forward (P46). Whether anything followed between late 2011 and the 2018–2019 case is still not established in the material read, and the question is kept open for that period.
Links: 1, 3.
v2.0 DS8 extension: EFTA00013587 documents the victim-notification
mechanics whose failure OPR later called poor judgment (see new
Story 25, the OPR investigation — the accountability counterpart).

v3.2 (WS5) extension — NPA-negotiation paper (NONPROSECUTION sample): EFTA00067260 (DS8): "CONFIDENTIAL PLEA NEGOTIATIONS — TERMS OF EPSTEIN NON-PROSECUTION AGREEMENT": Epstein pleads guilty (not nolo contendere) to an Information filed by the Palm Beach County State Attorney charging lewd and lascivious battery on a child, in violation of Fl. Stat. — a 1-page negotiation terms sheet. EFTA00013521 (DS8, Oct 31, 2007): AUSA email to Jay Lefkowitz re NPA paragraph 8 ("we are beginning to think about what discovery we may need to take to verify any claims"). EFTA00013968 (DS8, Jun 19, 2008): AUSA email re speaking with Roy Black about resolving the federal and state litigation. EFTA00014110 (DS8, Nov 24, 2008): USAO letter to Roy Black re Epstein. Post-NPA correspondence. EFTA00214042 / EFTA00214043 (DS9, Aug 18, 2009): AUSA email chain responding to a book/documentary author's inquiry: "There are no documents that were filed in connection with this case except some sealed matters. We deferred prosecution in favor of the state's prosecution of Epstein." A contemporaneous (Aug 2009) AUSA statement of the deferral posture.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — breach pre-history + 2010–2011 aftermath (the endpoint, the Jun 12, 2009 declaration, is unchanged): Jun 9, 2009 — "Operation Leap Year: Notification of Breach" memo (Sloman, Acting USA) (EFTA00189787, 14 pp.): seeks approval to serve the breach notice at the Jun 12, 2009 Marra hearing; recommends "proceed to indictment promptly thereafter" (no federal indictment followed in 2009 — the recommendation's outcome is not established in the memo); case-by-case survey of 13 civil suits and the breach theory (the most conservative reading of the NPA requires Epstein to waive challenges to liability where the plaintiff proceeds exclusively under 18 U.S.C. § 2255). Nov 26, 2008 — USAO letter: "Mr. Epstein has not breached the Non-Prosecution Agreement… by serving a portion of his 18-month sentence of imprisonment in the Palm Beach County Work Release Program" (EFTA00178359) — the pre-breach position the Second Addendum later superseded. The "SECOND ADDENDUM TO NON-PROSECUTION AGREEMENT" (EFTA00216077): recitals (NPA Sep 24, 2007; Addendum Oct 29, 2007; USAO gave notice it considers current work-release participation a material breach; Epstein disputes breach); new ¶2(a): consecutive 12 + 6 months county jail, no withholding/probation/community control; confined 24 h/day to the Stockade except work release from Mar 24, 2009 under PBSO rules (≤48 hours/week outside, GPS + deputy escort, work log weekly to USAO); breach of any condition allows the US to terminate the Agreement and prosecute Epstein "and any other individual or entity for any and all federal offenses." Signature blocks present; the Dated: lines are blank in the text layer — date of execution NOT established from this copy. Sep 26, 2011 — internal USAO thread re CVRA relief: "Setting aside the non-pros and prosecuting him as though the Non-pros had never been signed"; the Jane Does' desired relief was to set aside the NPA; a USAO voice argued Epstein "already served his sentence in state court and performed all his other obligations under the Non-Pros (including paying damages to 30-some girls)" and it would be a Due Process violation to suggest setting it aside (EFTA00205768 — shared with P1). The 2010–2011 investigation legs (shared with new story P46, where the episode is told whole): Oct 21, 2010 — Cassell to USAO: in late Jul 2010, Mike Fisten and others met the FBI re Epstein's sexual abuse of "other young girls — girls not covered by the non-prosecution agreement"; USAO reply: "Interviews have been conducted of potential new victims. Let me check in with the case agent and get back to you" (EFTA00206650). All of this is the victim's reported account as relayed by Edwards/Fisten to the AUSA in a preliminary-investigation memo; the AUSA states a formal memo with analysis is to follow. No finding is recorded in it. Cite only with that framing. Mar 24, 2011 — Daily Beast email to Roy Black: the Daily Beast received a letter from former US Attorney Alex Acosta describing the NPA negotiations; per the Daily Beast's summary, Acosta's letter says Epstein's defense team (a) negotiated in bad faith, agreeing to terms then appealing to DOJ in Washington; (b) investigated prosecutors' personal lives/families to discredit/disqualify two prosecutors — attempt failed; (c) threatened Acosta that his "excessive zeal" could become a book (EFTA00664159 — cite as the Daily Beast's summary of Acosta's letter, not as the letter itself). v3.3 (WS1) extension — Wild decisions + joint statement + notification record (record extended to Apr 15, 2021): *In re Wild*, 994 F.3d 1244 (11th Cir. 2021) (en banc, Apr 15, 2021) (EFTA00074599, 69 pp.) — held the CVRA "did not create a private right of action authorizing a crime victim to file stand-alone civil lawsuit to enforce CVRA rights"; petition denied; district court had found a CVRA violation (359 F. Supp. 3d 1201) but after Epstein's death the requested remedies were denied and the action dismissed (41 F. Supp. 3d 1321); dissent by Branch, J., joined by Martin, Jill Pryor, Hull, JJ. May 28, 2020 — email re *In re Wild*, 955 F.3d 1196 (11th Cir. 2020) (panel) (EFTA00016451, DS8, 1 p.): CVRA rights "do not attach until criminal proceedings have been initiated against a defendant, either by complaint, information, or indictment"; because the government never filed charges and entered an NPA, "the CVRA was never triggered." Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts (CVRA case) (EFTA00191264, 132 pp.) — stipulated facts: (1) between ~2001–2006 Epstein "sexually abused [and] enticed into prostitution minor girls" at his West Palm Beach mansion and elsewhere, incl. Jane Does #1 and #2; §2422 violations; (2) 2006 FBI opened the investigation at PBPD's request; girls 13–17; (4) Jun 7, 2007 FBI hand-delivered a CVRA victim notification letter to Jane Doe #1 promising "best efforts" incl. "reasonable right to confer" and "to be reasonably heard at any public proceeding… involving plea"; (5) Aug 11, 2007 same for Jane Doe #2; (6) Jane Doe #2 was represented by counsel paid for by Epstein; "openly hostile to the investigation… told investigators that she was not a victim… Epstein was an 'awesome man'… would consider marrying Epstein… actively avoided law enforcement… contacted other potential witnesses and victims to advise them against cooperating." (The text layer shows strike-throughs — a redlined draft of the joint statement; cite the stipulated facts as stated.) DRAFT government reply to petitioners' summary-judgment motion (EFTA01100373, 5 pp.): "Any failure to notify or consult were not the result of any 'conspiracy' with JE, nor any bad faith by the Government: they were the result of the USAO following the nationwide DOJ policy" reinforced by a Dec 17, 2010 OLC memorandum opinion (CVRA rights attach when criminal proceedings are initiated; cease if charges dismissed or government declines to bring formal charges after complaint); CVRA amended May 29, 2015 (§3771(a)(9) — right to be informed of a plea bargain/deferred prosecution agreement; "still does not clearly require CVRA rights to apply in the absence of a federal plea agreement or in circumstances where there is a federal Non-Prosecution Agreement"). A DRAFT — cite as the draft reply's argument. Nov 27, 2007 — Jay Lefkowitz (Epstein counsel) → USAO (EFTA00210517, 1 p.): objects to victim notification under the Justice for All Act; §2255 is a civil remedy, not restitution; "we had offered to provide a restitution fund for the alleged victims in this matter; however that option was rejected by your Office" (Epstein's side offered a restitution fund; USAO rejected it, per the letter); requests postponement of notification until after the plea + Starr/Fisher meeting. Jul 2008 USAO email production (EFTA00179991, 168 pp.): Jul 18, 2008 — "our victim notification letter has been filed in court… About 10 letters have gone out so far. The FBI's victim coordinator is updating the addresses on the rest and they will go out on Monday." Aug 1, 2008 — victims' counsel → USAO (EFTA00014125, DS8, 2 pp.): proposes stipulations for the CVRA case: (3) the NPA precludes federal charges for federal sex crimes against the victims; (4) the NPA "was negotiated… in September 2007 (and amended twice more during that year), the victims and their attorneys were not told about the non-prosecution agreement until after June 30, 2008, because of an express confidentiality provision in the agreement that the U.S. Attorney's Office, the FBI, and other federal agents all complied with." Also: Jul 9, 2008 AUSA sent a victim notification to Jane Doe #1 via Edwards. Jul 19, 2011 — USAO (Ferrer) → Roy Black (EFTA00205954, 1 p.): on Jul 17, 2011 the Office received a written request from the Manhattan DA for a copy of the signed NPA + the list of identified victims; per 5 U.S.C. §552a(b)(7) the Office intends to disclose to ADA Deborah L. Morse at 5:00 p.m. Jul 21, 2011; notice per NPA terms. Sep 26, 2011 — the set-aside debate (EFTA00205768, shared with Story 2): internal USAO thread re CVRA relief — "Setting aside the non-pros and prosecuting him as though the Non-pros had never been signed"; the Jane Does' desired relief was to set aside the NPA. Sep 2008 — "Respondent's Opposition to Victims' Motion to Unseal Non-Prosecution Agreement" (EFTA00204641, DS9, 7 pp., shared with P30): the NPA "was never filed in the instant case by the United States, either under seal or otherwise"; Aug 14, 2008 telephonic hearing; Aug 21, 2008 Order to Compel Production and Protective Order (DE 26); the government advised the court the Agreement had three parts: (1) Sep 2007 NPA, (2) Oct 2007 addendum, (3) a letter from the US Attorney to Epstein's attorneys suggesting a further modification; Epstein's attorneys contended the Agreement comprised only parts one and two.

It seeks to interview H.R.H. Prince Andrew Albert Christian Edward, the Duke of York (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor) relating to TWO ongoing criminal investigations, and records of certain communications and meetings between Prince Andrew and the subjects of one investigation. What was asked: a voluntary interview conducted by U.S. authorities in the presence of UK authorities (Attachment A questions); if the witness declines, a COMPELLED interview under oath, audio- or video-recorded, with a stated caution (treaty subpoena; right to remain silent where an answer would incriminate; anything said may be used against him; false statements prosecutable in the UK); and, if relevant information is provided, whether he would testify in future U.S. criminal proceedings in SDNY. Drafting and sending: revised draft circulated March 30, 2020 (EFTA00032129, "Material_Witness_PA_3.30_DRAFT_UK_MLAT_request.docx"); "final approved version" sent April 3, 2020, 7:30 p.m. (EFTA00037454), with delivery planned for Tuesday April 7 after discussions with the Deputy Chief of Mission, the Ambassador (only if he requests), and the Home Office, and "no public announcements about the delivery of the request until after the witness declines a voluntary interview." The same April 16, 2020 thread records internal confusion: an official had told the front office a report of the MLAT was false and then had to clarify. A signed final ("Material_Witness_PA_4.02_Final sigmed.pdf") was circulated for reference June 25, 2020 (EFTA00029796). Follow-up (EFTA00031512, June 26–30, 2020): the State Department asked to modify the confidentiality language; SDNY discussed Touhy/FOIA restrictions on the 302 and notes of any interview ("Absent a court order directing otherwise, the SDNY or FBI will not use or disclose the content of the witness's statements…"); and "The FBI should really understand that any leak of any of this would be pretty terrible." with no further identifying information — the name occurs once

second Lawrence H. Summers appears anywhere in the searched material.

identity NOT established. A shared exact name (including middle
initial) plus a shared orbit is not an identification under §6. Do
not conflate; do not merge P19's Summers into P12. What would decide
it: a probate filing, executor-qualification paper, or correspondence
naming the successor executor with an identifier; or a document
showing a different Lawrence H. Summers in Epstein's orbit.

The TD production itself was stamped Aug 2020, so the Sep 2019 stop is a property of the statements produced, not of the production date.

Span: Sep 17–24, 2012.
Anchor: main 26929 (Sep 18, 2012, Lesley Groff→Nili, subject "Jeffrey Epstein"): "Hi Nili... Jeffrey says he is free to meet with Ehud anytime from Friday Sept. 21st onwards... so what ever is most convenient for Ehud!... does not need to be Monday 24th.. please do let me know what suits his schedule best and we will do it." Quoted inside, Nili→Groff, Sep 18, 11:30 AM: "Hi lesley, first we would like a solo meeting with Jeffrey before Monday. On Monday o.k. around noon. We fly back at 5 p.m. Best Nili." (Friday Sep 21 and Monday Sep 24, 2012 check out as the calendar dates for that week.) New York is implied by "we fly back at 5 p.m."; the city is not named in the row.
Endpoint / dated stopping point: Sep 24, 2012 — the arrangement arc runs to the scheduled noon gathering at the Regency Hotel, Room 1131; completion is still NOT established (no post-event record in the sweep; no Sep 25 follow-up found; the Monday-afternoon messages still speak of the noon meeting prospectively and the Friday 8:14 PM instruction postdates its own 5 PM slot — both tensions flagged, not resolved). The Sep 2012 messages are DOJ-only: '1131' scores 0 hits across all five Barak DBs and no Sep 2012 Regency message is in the leak mailbox. The v3.2 'no follow-up found' is superseded by the v3.3 WS2 DS11 sweep below; the v3.2 DOJ cross-check's inconclusive result is replaced by the sweep's dated cluster.
Why it matters: this is the earliest documented Epstein contact in the mailbox, ~8 months before the atlas's earliest (Apr 22, 2013, main 27747, Epstein's Summers introduction; May 9, 2013, the Putin proposal, leak id 28024). The Barak–Epstein relationship evidently predates May 2013 in the mailbox record. It does not change Story 18 (the paid arrangement, Nov–Dec 2013) or Story 12 (May 2013–Feb 2019) — it is a separate, earlier prologue leg, reported as its own probable story (coordinator's placement decision; see changelog §1).
Tier: probable, not confirmed — a meeting was arranged in writing by both sides' schedulers; whether it took place is not in rows read. A schedule is never a held event (Standard rule 3). Links: Story 12, Story 18.
v3.3-corrected (Nov 6, 2026): classification reviewed after external review — P43 stays a standalone probable story (see changelog §11). The arrangement chain meets the atlas definition and the v1.3 P13 precedent: the arrangement itself is the documented decision, ending at the explicit dated stopping point Sep 24, 2012. It is not a fragment (a week-long arc across 15 contents, not a single scheduling memo) and not a Story 12 extension (the eight-month gap to Apr/May 2013 has no connecting document).
Verification (v3.2, WS3): document-level verified — anchor body-read in full.

v3.3 (WS2) extension — the DS11 Sep-2012 sweep: the DOJ-side follow-through is now documented (15 distinct contents; 18 IDs incl. 3 duplicate copies). Windows searched: `data_set : 11 AND "September 2012"` → 22 docs (all 22 triaged by head; none mentions Barak); `data_set : 11 AND Groff AND Barak AND September` → 43 docs (all triaged by head); Bates-range windows EFTA02559000–EFTA02562000 (2,212 docs, 26 keyword hits), EFTA02558000–EFTA02559000 (715 docs, 0 Sep-2012 Barak hits), EFTA02562000–EFTA02563000 (746 docs, 0), EFTA02700000–EFTA02703000 (2,020 docs; 2 hits, both cluster duplicates). Leak-mailbox check: "Regency" and "1131" across all five Barak DBs — no Sep 2012 Regency message in the leak mailbox ("1131" scores 0 everywhere). **The cluster is DOJ-only material.** In chronological order, all Groff→Epstein unless noted: Sep 17–18, 2012 — Epstein↔Larry Summers: Epstein (Mon Sep 17, 5:05 PM): "22-24". Summers (Sep 17, 3:36 PM): "When. I'm in Korea right now." Epstein (Tue Sep 18, 5:34 AM): "any interest in Ehud, at my house". Reply at the top of the chain (Tue Sep 18, 12:32 AM; sender blank in the text layer): "Will be in nyc on 24 mostly free." (EFTA02560037 — direct Epstein–Summers contact about Barak; also the P12 leg.) Tue Sep 18, 2012, 3:37 PM — "Barak/Larry Summers" (EFTA02559810): "Barak says he would like a solo meeting with you on Monday Sept. 24th at noon and he flies back at 5pm. What time do you want Larry Summers to join? Should this be a lunch?" — Groff relaying Nili's message; the mirror of main 26929, with the new element that Larry Summers was to join at some point. Tue Sep 18, 2012, 3:51 PM — "Barak — tell me exactly please" (EFTA02559880): "Please tell me exactly what you would like me to ask Nili for when it comes to Barak… 'A solo meeting with you and Barak sometime Sat, Sun or Mon, whenever convenient for him, possibly for a meal or just coffee'" — Epstein's instruction to Groff, 14 minutes after the previous message. Thu Sep 20, 2012, 11:41 AM — "Barak" (EFTA02559941): forwards Nili (Thu Sep 20, 6:49 AM): "ehud will be back from washington tomorrow friday around 4 pm, will jeffrey be so kind as to come over to the hotel (regency on park avenue and 61st… as flights are imprevisible, i shall call you upon his arrival so jeffrey won't be waiting. please confirm". **The plan shifts: Friday Sep 21, Epstein to come to Barak's hotel after ~4 PM.** Fri Sep 21, 2012, 11:41 AM — "Schedule" (EFTA02561234; duplicate copy EFTA02701667, same remote-id 247046, same timestamp; the copy adds "3:00 Nina Keita"): Friday schedule: "11:00 Katya; 11:30; 12:30 Lunch with Steven Kosslyn; 1:30 conf call with Kosslyn's attorneys; 3:00; **5:15 Go See Barak at Regency**; 7:00 Dinner with Michael Wood." **The Barak visit is on Epstein's calendar for Friday 5:15 PM.** Fri Sep 21, 2012, 1:58 PM — "Barak Regency Room #1131" (EFTA02560908): "Barak is in Room room no. 1131 at the Regency Hotel, Park Ave & 61st." Fri Sep 21, 2012, 8:14 PM — "JE to be AT REGENCY AT 5pm — Rm#1131" (EFTA02560494, to Janusz Banasiak and Richard Barnett, Epstein CC'd): "Jeffrey is to be at the Regency at 5pm. Park Ave and 61st. Room 1131." (Sent at 8:14 PM, after the 5 PM slot — reported as written; see below.) Sun Sep 23, 2012, 8:59 PM — "Has Barak meeting been moved to 11am?" (EFTA02561225): "Have you heard if 11am will work for tomorrow with Barak? Larry Summers' assistants are asking because they need to change his airline tickets. Please advise." Mon Sep 24, 2012 — "Larry Summers" (EFTA02560633; duplicate copy EFTA02366153, same remote-id 247637, same text): "I confirmed with Larry Summers assistants you will meet Larry in the lobby of the Regency at 11am today." Mon Sep 24, 2012, 12:29 PM — "9:15 Karyna/Janusz" (EFTA02559879): "Janusz is a bit concerned about being back in time to get you to the Regency from dropping Karyna at school this morning. Should Karyna leave earlier than 9:15 for school to ensure Janusz is back in plenty of time for you?" — Epstein being driven to the Regency that day. Mon Sep 24, 2012, 1:56 PM — "Reid confirmed 11:45 in room" (EFTA02560130): "Reid has confirmed he will be at the room at the Regency at 11:45 today. Regency Hotel, Park Ave & 61st, Room 1131." "Reid" — surname not stated in the document (Reid Hoffman, who appears elsewhere in the atlas, is a candidate; the document does not establish the identification). Mon Sep 24, 2012, 3:05 PM — "Joe Pagano" (EFTA02560251; duplicate copy EFTA02701903, same timestamp/text): "Joe Pagano asked where he is to meet you at noon… he thought he was to come to the house… I told [name unclear in text layer] you will be at the Regency at noon… FYI — Nili has not responded to my email asking if ok for Joe Pagano to come at noon…" Mon Sep 24, 2012, 3:07 PM — "Nili! re Joe Pagano" (EFTA02560282): "Nili says 'we count on Jeffrey-ok' re would it be ok for Joe Pagano to come along as well at noon today.." Mon Sep 24, 2012, 3:08 PM — "Joe Pagano will be in lobby at 11:50" (EFTA02560305): "Joe says he will be in the lobby at the Regency at 11:50 so you don't have to wait on him…" (A phone number follows in the document; not reproduced here, per the Standard's no-PII rule.) Mon Sep 24, 2012, 2:39 PM — Ian Osborne→Epstein, "Re: What's the plan at 12 today?" (EFTA02560221): "Great, I will see you there." Quoting Epstein (Sep 24): "You and a few friends regency hotel 12 rm 1131". **Epstein's own words placing the noon gathering at the Regency, Room 1131, with "a few friends".** What the sweep establishes: the arrangement did not end with main 26929. The DOJ side carries the negotiation forward day by day: the Monday-noon solo plan (Sep 18) → a Friday-afternoon hotel visit plan (Sep 20) → the Friday 5:15 PM calendar entry and the Regency Room 1131 logistics (Sep 21) → the Sunday-evening open question about moving Monday to 11 AM (Sep 23) → the Monday convergence: Summers in the lobby at 11 AM, Reid at the room at 11:45, Pagano in the lobby at 11:50, Epstein expected at noon in Room 1131, with Nili's "we count on Jeffrey-ok" for Pagano joining. The venue is established (Regency Hotel, Park Ave & 61st, Room 1131); Larry Summers' participation is established as planned (invited Sep 17–18, lobby meeting 11 AM Sep 24); Ian Osborne's attendance is established as planned (Epstein's own message). **Completion is still NOT established** — no document in the sweep records the meeting as having taken place: no debrief, no thank-you, no "good meeting" note, no Sep 25 follow-up (`Barak AND "September 25"` → 0; `Regency AND "September 25"` → 0). Two cautions against over-reading: (a) the Friday 8:14 PM instruction "JE to be AT REGENCY AT 5pm" (EFTA02560494) was sent *after* the 5 PM slot it names; (b) the Monday 3:05–3:08 PM messages (EFTA02560251/282/305) still speak of the noon meeting prospectively ("would it be ok for Joe Pagano to come along as well at noon today"), which sits oddly against a noon start — the timestamps are reported as the documents state them and the tension is flagged, not resolved. A schedule is never a held event (Standard rule 3). **P43 stays probable, not confirmed.** The story's shape changes from "single exchange, no follow-up" to "a week-long arrangement arc with a scheduled venue and converging attendees, completion not established." Placement: P43 stays its own probable story — the new material strengthens it without merging it into Story 12; the eight-month gap to Apr/May 2013 still has no connecting document. Duplicate copies are cited as copies (same remote-id), not independent corroboration.

stories.entry_markdown:
Span: May 7 – Jul 17, 2013.
Anchors: main 27908 (May 7, 2013, Jack Bendheim→Barak, CC Jonathan): "Ehud when u have 15 minutes I would appreciate it if you could sit with Jonathan to discuss a project." Barak replies (same day, in-chain): "jack, i'll do. where is he? I'll be in IL in Shavouth. In NY this Sat for few hrs."; main 27915 (May 8, 2013, Jonathan→Barak, CC Jack): "Please let me know what dates/times would work for you to meet in Israel and I will make one of the times work."; main 27926 (May 22, 2013, Jonathan→Barak): "I wanted to thank you again for taking the time to meet with me and Anshel on Friday" — the meeting was held (Friday May 17, 2013). Follow-up: Barak asked Jonathan to reach out to Ziv Lautenberg and to "walk Doron through the offering"; Jonathan asks Barak "to once again consider getting involved with business in whatever capacity you see fit. While it has taken time for Nowforce.com to build a strong and sustainable platform, the business [is] finally at a stage where it is ready to significantly accelerate its growth and take advantage of the very real global opportunity that exists for our solution."; main 31158 (Jul 17, 2013, Barak→Jonathan, quoting the May 22–29 chain): Barak's May 22 reply — "Thanks. Will discuss it again during the wedding. In the meantime try to talk to Danny Yatom former head of Mossad and CoS to me. He runs a security co. which might help in promoting it. I've told him about your co." — and Jonathan's May 29 report: "we had a meeting with Danny Yatom and his son at their office. We agreed on next steps for him to make introductions with some of his relationships in relevant orgs/people in the US. Thank you again for making the introduction." Barak, Jul 17: "Jonathan Thx. Yatom is very practical. VG. EB".
Endpoint / dated stopping point: Jul 17, 2013 (Barak's endorsement of Yatom). Barak's own involvement with Nowforce itself is NOT established in rows read. "Nowforce" totals 3 main hits + 2 Hyperion hits across all five DBs; nothing after Jul 17, 2013. Whether Barak ever engaged, and what Yatom's introductions produced, would need sources outside this mailbox.
Tier: probable, not confirmed — the chain is real (introduction → completed meeting → documented follow-through to Yatom), but the story's natural endpoint (whether Barak got involved with Nowforce, and what Yatom's introductions produced) is not in rows read. Business/association record, not an allegation. People: Ehud Barak, Jack C. Bendheim (introducer), Jonathan Bendheim, "Anshel" (meeting attendee, surname not in rows read), Danny Yatom (former head of Mossad and Barak's former chief of staff, per Barak's May 22 message), Ziv Lautenberg (Barak's former son-in-law, per Jonathan's May 22 message), "Doron" (surname not in rows read). Links: Story 14 (same 2013 investment orbit; distinct arc, kept separate).
Verification (v3.2, WS3): document-level verified — anchors body-read in full.

v3.3 (WS2) extension — outside-the-mailbox chase (clean negative on follow-through, with two incidental DOJ mentions and one identity candidate): **No Nowforce/Yatom/Barak follow-through was found outside the mailbox: no contract, no funding, no dated end.** Whether Barak ever engaged with Nowforce, and what Yatom's introductions produced, remain not established — now after a DOJ-wide and HO search, not just a mailbox search. What was searched (DOJ corpus, all sets; House Oversight): `Nowforce` → **2 docs** (EFTA02370081 DS11; EFTA01074376 DS9), HO **0**; `Bendheim` → **13 docs** (1 DS9, 12 DS10), HO **0**; `Yatom` → **1 doc** (EFTA00973971 DS9), HO **40 pages** — all Barak's memoir (Danny Yatom as his Sayeret deputy/security aide), duplicated across Parts 1 and 9; no Nowforce content; `Goldwasser` → 10 docs, 0 in DS11, none Benad; `"Shanghai Alliance"` → **0**. This is a clean negative **stating what was searched**, not an absolute negative: absence in the searched material proves only absence in the searched material. The two DOJ "Nowforce" hits: EFTA01074376 (DS9, 40 pp.) — Reporty Homeland Security Ltd, Business Plan 2014: the single "NowForce" mention sits in a market-products list (p. 26) — a comparable-company listing inside the Reporty plan, not a Nowforce follow-through (shared with Story 20, where the plan is the leg); EFTA02370081 (DS11, 3 pp.) — AFHU E-Connections newsletter, sent Tue Jul 8, 2014: "Anshel Pfeffer, a Hebrew University alumnus, co-founded NowForce, which provides mobile solutions for emergency response organizations." Press/newsletter content only — no Barak, Bendheim, Yatom, contract, or funding. **The "Anshel" identity candidate (NOT confirmed):** P44's meeting attendee is "Anshel" (surname not in rows read). **"Anshel" occurs exactly once in the entire DOJ corpus: EFTA02370081, as "Anshel Pfeffer".** That document also states Pfeffer co-founded NowForce — the company whose pitch meeting P44's "Anshel" attended with Jonathan Bendheim on Fri May 17, 2013. Proposed reading (candidate, not confirmed): P44's "Anshel" is Anshel Pfeffer. The evidence is circumstantial but specific: same first name, same company, and the only "Anshel" in 1.38M DOJ documents. Per Standard rule 6 this is **not** asserted as an identification — the documents do not state it, and the two items come from different source families (leak mailbox vs. DOJ newsletter). Carry both readings: "Anshel (surname not in rows read; 'Anshel Pfeffer', named as NowForce co-founder in a Jul 8, 2014 newsletter, EFTA02370081, is a candidate identification, not established)." The other hits, all checked: the 13 Bendheim docs are unrelated Bendheims (Deutsche Bank statements with income distributions to "KATHY BENDHEIM" / "THOMAS L BENDHEIM" / "CATHERINE L BENDHEIM" — EFTA01255960, EFTA01299408, EFTA01299483, EFTA01299542; client/trust lists naming "BENDHEIM, JOHN M", "Bendheim, Andrew", "Bendheim Jr., John M." — EFTA01398754, EFTA01398949, EFTA01460973; four copies of one Deutsche Bank questionnaire about "Andrew J Bendheim" — EFTA01456920, EFTA01456922, EFTA01456930, EFTA01472504, EFTA01472507, EFTA01472510 — EFTA01472510 clarifies "our client is Jeffrey Epstein per the subject line and not Andrew J Bendheim as you mentioned in question #2"). **No Jack Bendheim, no Jonathan Bendheim, no Nowforce, no Yatom in any of the 13.** EFTA00973971 (DS9, 24 pp.) — a Daily Beast article quoting "Danny Yatom, a former chief of Israel's intelligence service, the Mossad, in an interview" about Turkish intelligence burning agents to Iran. Press quote; no Nowforce, Barak, or Bendheim link. (The Bendheim/Yatom noise IDs are recorded here as checked-and-not-added; they are not anchors and are not in the JSON.)

v3.3 (WS4) extension — fuller read of the DS11 Spinella core (330 openings; 14 in full). Anchors: EFTA02486657 (Oct 1, 2015, Richard Joslin → Epstein: "Use tax payable @ 9/30/15 — 2015 acquisitions LDB= 1.55 million Narrows $2.5 million. Use tax paid 4/15 $1.9 million (with extension)." The payment schedule is as follows: 1. $23 million paid on May 12, 2015 2. $34.5 million due on June 30, 2015 3. $28.75 million due on October 1, 2015 4. New York State & City sales tax of $10,206,250 due in February 2016 upon transfer of title to and possession of the Work to Leon 5. $28.75 million due on April 15, 2016… Leon has emphasized to me several times how very confidential this purchase is").
Endpoint / dated stopping point: Oct 1, 2015 — the Joslin email recording use tax payable as of Sep 30, 2015; the last dated document in the chain. Documented as paid: $23M on May 12, 2015 (Gray's schedule, item 1) and $1.9M use tax paid Apr 15, 2015 (Joslin: "Use tax paid 4/15 $1.9 million (with extension)"). The remaining instalments are schedule only — $34.5M due Jun 30, 2015; $28.75M due Oct 1, 2015; $28.75M due Apr 15, 2016; $10,206,250 NY sales tax due Feb 2016 — payment of each is NOT established in this document. Title/possession: SCHEDULED for transfer in Feb 2016 (Gray's item 4 makes the Feb 2016 sales tax due "upon transfer of title to and possession of the Work to Leon"); the transfer itself is NOT established — no document in this filing records it as having occurred. A payment deadline is not a payment, and a scheduled transfer is not a transfer (Standard rule 3). Handled through Elysium Management with Epstein's team doing the use-tax work; Gray's note stresses Leon's insistence on confidentiality. "LDB" and "Narrows" (use-tax lines in the same filing) are not identified beyond the document's wording.
Tier: probable, not confirmed — single-document anchor (two emails inside one filing); needs a second source family for confirmed. Business/association record, not an allegation. People: Leon Black, Heather Gray (Elysium Management), Richard Joslin. Links: P45 (the same filing is a P45 leg — the use-tax work inside the Black advisory arc).
Verification (v3.3, WS4): document-level verified — anchor body-read in full. v3.3-corrected (Nov 6, 2026): endpoint moved Apr 15, 2016 → Oct 1, 2015 (the Apr 15, 2016 date was a payment deadline, not a documented event); title transfer restated as scheduled, not occurred — see changelog §11.
